tool_args.rationale: The pilot signatures favor normalized siphon forcing with a gradient sink and coupled memory. Every pilot endpoint is at least 72 characteristic fast timescales out, so the fit primarily sees the net effect of the transient rather than its evolution. The fine trajectory batch is the relevant probe for distinguishing the full coupled model from a reduced slow model before fresh confirmation.

considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: This is the leading model, but five endpoint observations at horizons far beyond the fast timescale do not reliably separate the fast relaxation, memory coupling, and slow damping.

considered_alternatives.option: Reduced slow ODE with a static gradient-dependent siphon
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: The fast state may be approximated at the target horizon, but the current data do not establish whether the transient from mem_conv can be dropped or absorbed into the initial condition without exceeding tolerance.
It does not resolve the ambiguity between transient memory and slow dynamics.
